chains.title: FOXA1 binds the alt T allele more strongly at a cryptic intronic enhancer and distally up-regulates PELI2

links.claim: The hypothesis posits that FOXA1 binds the alt T allele more strongly, but no QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific binding data are supplied for FOXA1 in this case; E04 reports no ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over this base in any biosample, including MCF-7, and E09 specifically reports no FOXA1 ChIP-seq peak in MCF-7. The binding claim is therefore speculative and unsupported.

The variant would have to create or alter a cryptic FOXA1-responsive enhancer; E01 shows an intronic variant with GERP -3.12, not evidence of conservation, and E03 shows no overlapping cCRE, with the nearest dELS 1868 bp away. No cryptic enhancer activity or allele-dependent regulatory effect is demonstrated.

The cryptic enhancer would distally up-regulate PELI2, the nearest protein-coding gene at 230.8 kb; this long-range linkage is unproven. E02 gives linear distance only, E07 reports no significant GTEx v8 eQTL for this variant, and E06 is a weak brain molecular QTL for a different non-coding gene ENSG00000259868 (PIP 0.03), not PELI2 in MCF-7.

The proposed effect occurs in MCF-7 breast-cancer cells, but E04 reports no ENCODE TF ChIP-seq peak over this base in MCF-7 and E09 reports no FOXA1 ChIP-seq peak in MCF-7; FOXA1 occupancy and allele-specific activity in this cell type are not demonstrated.

PELI2 dysregulation is proposed to contribute to breast cancer. E08a supports Pellino-family E3 ubiquitin-ligase identity, E08b lists PELI2 among prognostic genes in papillary thyroid carcinoma, E08c concerns tramadol in breast cancer cells without PELI2, and E08d concerns BRCA1. None establishes PELI2 dysregulation as contributing to breast cancer at this locus.
